extracted.intended_audience: Participating Federal Agencies and small business applicants (SBCs)
extracted.subtask_description: Policy directive guidance for operating SBIR and STTR programs, including eligibility, phased award structure (Phase I/II/III), data rights, solicitation/competition rules, pilot programs, agency responsibilities, and commercialization considerations for award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency compliance with Policy Directive
rubrics_metrics.description: The SBIR/STTR Policy Directive outlines how agencies must generally conduct their programs. When incorporating SBIR/STTR policy into agency-specific regulations and procedures, Participating Agencies may develop and apply processes needed to implement the policy effectively; however, no Participating Agency may develop and apply policies, directives, or clauses, that contradict, weaken, or conflict with the policy as stated in the directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Participating Agency is required to review its rules, policies, and guidance on the programs to ensure consistency with this Policy Directive and to make any necessary changes in accordance with each agency's normal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory participation thresholds and set-asides
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Federal agency with an extramural budget for R/R&D in excess of $100,000,000 must participate in the SBIR program and spend a minimum percentage of their extramural R/R&D budgets (3.2% in FY2017 and statutory percentage thereafter). Each Federal agency with an extramural budget for R/R&D in excess of $1,000,000,000 must participate in the STTR program and spend a minimum percentage (0.45% in FY2016 and statutory percentage thereafter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal agency may exceed these minimum percentages. Participating Agencies must report to SBA on the calculation of the agency’s extramural R/R&D budget within four months of enactment of each agency’s annual Appropriations Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform three-phase award process
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, each Participating Agency must make SBIR/STTR awards for R/R&D through the following uniform, three-phase process: Phase I (determine scientific/technical merit and feasibility), Phase II (further develop Phase I work that meets program needs and has commercial potential), Phase III (commercial applications or follow-on work funded by non-SBIR/STTR sources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must issue SBIR/STTR awards pursuant to competitive and merit-based selection procedures. Agencies may not use investment of venture capital, hedge funds, or private equity as an award criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I objective and evaluation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase I involves solicitation of proposals to conduct feasibility-related experimental or theoretical R/R&D. The object is to determine the scientific and technical merit and feasibility of the proposed effort and the quality of performance of the SBC with a relatively small agency investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency criteria used to evaluate SBIR/STTR proposals must give consideration to the scientific and technical merit and feasibility of the proposal along with its potential for Commercialization; considerations may also include program balance with respect to market or technological risk or critical agency requirements. Agency benchmarks for progress towards Commercialization must be met to be eligible to participate in Phase I. Agencies may require submission of Phase II proposal as a Phase I deliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II objective and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of Phase II is to continue the R/R&D effort from the completed Phase I. Unless exceptions apply, only Phase I awardees are eligible for Phase II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must base its decision upon the results of work performed under the Phase I award and the scientific and technical merit and commercial potential of the Phase II proposal. Agencies may not use an invitation, pre-screening, or pre-selection process for Phase II eligibility; solicitations must note that all Phase I awardees may apply for Phase II and provide guidance on the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II award selection considerations (commercial potential evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II award decisions require consideration of a proposal's commercial potential, including potential to transition to private sector, Government, or Government contractor applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial potential may be evidenced by the SBC's record of successfully commercializing research; existence of Phase II funding commitments from private/non-SBIR sources; existence of Phase III follow-on commitments; and other indicators of commercial potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II guideline amounts and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase II awards have guideline amounts and limits (each Phase II has a guideline amount of $1 million and a limit of $1.5 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special/supplementary awards (e.g., Phase IIB) linked to a base Phase II aggregate with the base Phase II to determine total SBIR/STTR funds; NIH Phase IIB handled as sequential Phase II subject to these guideline amounts and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III definition and status
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase III refers to work that derives from, extends, or completes an effort made under prior SBIR/STTR Funding Agreements, but is funded by sources other than the SBIR/STTR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase III work includes commercial application financed by non-Federal capital, SBIR/STTR-derived products or services for the Federal Government funded by non-SBIR/STTR Federal funding, or continuation of SBIR/STTR work funded by non-SBIR/STTR Federal funding. A Phase III award must include SBIR/STTR Data Rights protection and has SBIR/STTR status.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Data Rights and Protection Period
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR/STTR Data Rights: the Government’s license rights in properly marked SBIR/STTR Data during the SBIR/STTR Protection Period. The SBIR/STTR Protection Period begins at award and ends not less than twenty years from that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the protection period the Government may use SBIR/STTR Data within the Government but shall not use, release, or disclose data for procurement, manufacture or commercial purposes without permission; release outside the Government requires conditions (e.g., NDA that complies with §8). Upon expiration, the Government has a royalty-free license to use and authorize others to use these Data for Government Purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Computer Software Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose SBIR/STTR Data that are Computer Software within the Federal Government for specified internal uses and distribution to another Government agency with notification and copy of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government shall not release, disclose, or permit access to SBIR/STTR Data that is Computer Software for commercial, manufacturing, or procurement purposes without the written permission of the Awardee. Release outside the Government requires an NDA that complies with §8 or limited exceptions for government support contractors or necessary essential government activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Technical Data Rights and external release
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may use and disclose SBIR/STTR Technical Data within the Federal Government, but shall not use, release, or disclose the data for procurement, manufacture or commercial purposes; or release or disclose the data outside the Government except as permitted by paragraph (2) or by written permission of the Awardee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical Data may be released outside the Federal Government only if the recipient entered into an NDA per §8 and the release is necessary for narrowly-tailored essential Government activities, to a Government support services contractor under conditions, to a foreign government if required to serve U.S. interests, or to non-Government entities for evaluation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and solicitation publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any federal executive agency intending to solicit a proposal to contract for property or services valued above FAR §5.101 thresholds must transmit a notice of the impending solicitation to the Government point of entry (GPE) and must not issue its solicitation for at least 15 days from the date of publication on the GPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers must generally make available through the GPE relevant solicitations, specifications, and pertinent information. Agencies must establish a submission deadline in accordance with FAR §5.203. Exemptions exist for certain Phase I contract solicitations in excess of $25,000 if a written determination is made after consulting OFPP and SBA that publication is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using venture capital/hedge/private equity ownership as award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may not use investment of venture capital or investment from hedge funds or private equity firms as a criterion for an SBIR/STTR award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and special provisions for 'Covered Small Business Concern' and associated registration/certification requirements are provided elsewhere in the directive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing and matching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing or matching funds cannot be required for Phase I or Phase II awards, but agencies may require a small business to have matching funds for certain special awards (e.g., to reduce the gap between a Phase II and Phase III award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific pilot programs and special awards may explicitly require matching funds and define eligible/ ineligible sources and required matching amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Assistance Pilot Program (third Phase II) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: SBCs may apply for a third Phase II award under a Commercialization Assistance Pilot Program; awards may be used for R/R&D activities that build on Phase II work and ensure rapid progress toward commercialization and require matching funding from eligible third parties equal to the award amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies shall consider extent award aids commercialization; whether updated commercialization plan provides a sound approach for establishing technical feasibility; whether proposed activities improve likelihood of societal benefits; whether SBC progressed satisfactorily in Phase II; expectations of the eligible third-party investor; and likelihood of leading to commercial and societal benefit. Eligible third-party investors and ineligible sources are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching funding eligibility and prohibitions for pilot awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching funding from an eligible third party is required for certain pilot programs and must equal the amount of the award. Eligible sources include another SBC, venture capital firms, individual investors, and non-SBIR federal/state/local governments. Ineligible sources include the SBC’s internal R&D funds, in-kind contributions, funding from owners/family/ affiliates, or funding attained through loans/debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching amounts exclude any fees collected by the SBC and must be provided in cash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of SBIR/STTR funds for Phase III and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase III work deriving from prior SBIR/STTR Funding Agreements must have SBIR/STTR Phase III status and SBIR/STTR Data Rights; Phase III awards do not require a new competition in order to satisfy competition statutes if derived from prior Phase I/II awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of Justification and Approval, it is sufficient to state the project is an SBIR/STTR Phase III award derived from prior SBIR/STTR agreements; further justification is not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of key eligibility and program terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive definitions provided for terms such as Act, Additionally Eligible State, Affiliate, Applicant, Awardee, Commercialization, Computer Database, Computer Programs, Computer Software, Covered Small Business Concern, Data, Essentially Equivalent Work, Extramural R/R&D Budget/Obligations, Federal Agency, Federal Laboratory, Form Fit and Function Data, Funding Agreement, Government Purpose, Innovation, Intellectual Property, Joint Venture, Key Individual, OMIT Data, Participating Agency, Principal Investigator/Project Manager, Program Solicitation, Prototype, Research Institution, R/R&D, SBIR/STTR Computer Software Rights, SBIR/STTR Data, SBIR/STTR Data Rights, SBIR/STTR Protection Period, SBIR/STTR Technical Data Rights, Small Business Concern (SBC), Student/Faculty-owned SBC, Subcontract, Technology Development Program, Technical Data, United States, Unlimited Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions govern eligibility, rights, responsibilities, and interpretations across the directive (see full glossary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies' reporting obligations to SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Agency shall provide information to SBA for SBA to monitor and analyze each agency’s SBIR/STTR program and to report annually to Congressional committees. Agencies must report on extramural budgets, solicitations, awards, and other specified operational features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating Agencies must report to SBA on the calculation of the agency’s extramural R/R&D budget within four months of enactment of each agency’s annual Appropriations Act; see §10 for reporting frequency and specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA monitoring, outreach, and data collection responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA establishes policy and procedures, collects program-wide data, maintains www.SBIR.gov, conducts outreach to educate the public, highlights successes, and monitors implementation of SBIR/STTR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA will monitor funding allocations, solicitation and award status, follow-on funding commitments, and ensure Participating Agencies maintain systems to minimize fraud, waste, and abuse. SBA defines performance areas and metrics and works with agencies to set measurable goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers and exceptions process
rubrics_metrics.description: Waivers providing limited exceptions to certain policies can be found at §10(k) of this Policy Directive. Agencies may request waivers for limited exceptions (e.g., subcontracting provision back to issuing agency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any agency seeking an exception must follow the waiver process set out in the directive and document consultations where required (e.g., OFPP and SBA consultation for certain solicitation publication exemptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program (civilian agencies) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A civilian Participating Agency (except DoD) may allocate not more than 10% of its SBIR funds for follow-on awards to support commercialization readiness. The agency must apply to SBA at least 90 days before the fiscal year with compelling reasons for additional investment. SBA must determine within 30 days and publish determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum award under this pilot may not exceed 3 times the Phase II guideline amounts. Awardees must register with SBA in Company Registry Database. Agencies must consider whether the technology is likely to be manufactured in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Readiness Program (DoD CRP) provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD and military departments may create and administer a CRP to accelerate transition of SBIR technologies to Phase III and acquisition. CRP authority doesn't replace other insertion/transition programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD may use SBIR funds for CRP administration in accordance with §9(e)(3). For contracts valued at not less than $100,000,000, DoD may set goals for Phase III transitions in subcontracting plans and require reporting on Phase III subcontracting; DoD must set goals to increase Phase II transitions into programs of record and report metrics to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 0 Proof of Concept Partnership Pilot Program (NIH) guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Director may use funds for a Proof of Concept Partnership Pilot Program to accelerate creation of small businesses and commercialization from qualifying institutions; grants to qualifying institutions up to $1,000,000 per year for up to 4 years to administer Proof of Concept Partnership awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining recipients, consider technology transfer/commercialization office, commitment to economic development, geographic and size diversity, ability to assemble project management boards with industry/venture experts, IP strategy, and sustainability plan. Proof of Concept Partnerships must use market-focused oversight (diverse review board, technology validation milestones focused on market feasibility, simple reporting to redirect projects, willingness to reallocate funding). No more than $100,000 to an individual proposal; funds not for basic research or unrelated equipment; funds may be used for validation, market research, IP clarity, and commercialization mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Development Program review authority
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency with a Technology Development Program may review for funding outreach/assistance proposals to help SBCs prepare SBIR proposals and may review meritorious Phase I proposals not funded due to fiscal constraints for SBCs in eligible states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the eligible Technology Development Programs (EPSCoR, DEPSCoR, IDeA, AFRI, etc.) relevant to specific agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on pilot program authorities and termination dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Several pilot program authorities (e.g., Commercialization Assistance Pilot Program, Commercialization Readiness Pilot Program, Phase 0 Proof of Concept Partnership Pilot Program) include statutory termination dates (notably referenced as terminating on September 30, 2022 unless extended) or other expiration mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow expiration/renewal rules and SBA determinations where applicable; the directive notes these terminations and any required SBA publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting back to issuing agency restriction and waiver requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Agencies must request a waiver to issue a Funding Agreement that includes a provision for subcontracting a portion of that agreement back to the issuing agency if there is no exception to this requirement in the directive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §9(e)(4) for further information on waiver process and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on duplicative funding and 'Essentially Equivalent Work'
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Essentially Equivalent Work' covers work substantially the same research proposed for funding in more than one proposal to same or different Federal Agencies, or work with same specific research objective and research design as another proposal or award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concept is used to prevent duplicative funding across proposals/awards and is a basis for eligibility and award decisions.
